stories.title: Astoria Favorite :3Coffee Roasters Expands to Halletts Point
stories.excerpt: The Durst Organization has signed :3Coffee Roasters to a 1,232-square-foot lease for a new retail location at 30 Halletts Point in Astoria, Queens. Expected to open later this year, the new shop marks an expansion for the family-owned business and its second Astoria location. It will also be the first retail at 20 and 30 Halletts Point, which opened last year with 647 apartments. “Halletts Point is a thriving community with spectacular views of Manhattan and Queens. As the neighborhood continues to grow, we are selecting retailers that will bring additional value to residents and neighbors alike, and we are excited to welcome :3Coffee Roasters,” said Jody Durst, President of The Durst Organization. :3Coffee Roasters was founded by Astoria residents Fabian Guzman and Andrea Gomez. The brand first opened on Steinway Street in Astoria and later expanded to the Flatiron District in Manhattan, building a following for their neighborhood-oriented approach and high-quality offerings. The Durst Organization was represented in-house by Karen Rose and Eric Engelhardt and by KSR’s Zach Nathan, Mark Gallucci, and Hunter Lazan. :3Coffee Roasters was represented by Genaro Otero at Sinvin. The post Astoria Favorite :3Coffee Roasters Expands to Halletts Point appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Durst Organization opens 647-unit Halletts Point apartment building in Astoria, Queens (2025).
First retail tenant :3Coffee Roasters signs 1,232 sq ft at 30 Halletts Point, opening later this year.
Family-owned coffee roaster expanding to second Astoria location; brand has Manhattan presence.
stories.summary: The Durst Organization's 647-unit Halletts Point residential development in Astoria, Queens, which opened last year, is now leasing its first retail space to :3Coffee Roasters, a neighborhood-focused brand already established in Astoria and the Flatiron. The 1,232-square-foot lease marks the project's first retail activation and the roaster's second Astoria location.
stories.impact: Retail activation at Halletts Point signals strong neighborhood stabilization and foot-traffic confidence in the mixed-use component, which typically drives resident retention and NOI in multifamily. Durst's ability to attract a locally-favored independent (not a chain) tenant suggests healthy demand fundamentals in Astoria and validates renter absorption in the 647-unit building; this de-risks future multifamily development in the Long Island City/Astoria corridor.

stories.title: CBRE Arranges Debt on Advanced Manufacturing Campus in San Jose’s Golden Triangle
stories.excerpt: CBRE announced it arranged $67.4 million in financing for Forge North First, a mixed-phase industrial/R&D campus and advanced manufacturing development in San Jose’s Golden Triangle submarket. Mike Walker, Brad Zampa, and Andy Gross of CBRE’s Debt & Structured Finance team in San Francisco arranged the five-year bridge loan with floating-rate, non-recourse financing from an institutional lender on behalf of Four Corners Properties and a West Coast-based institutional investor. “The combination of surging occupier demand and extremely limited supply positions Four Corners to create significant value at Forge North First,” said Zampa. Four Corners, an established local investor and developer founded in 2005, has invested in 50 buildings totaling 7.2 million square feet. In January 2026, Four Corners and its institutional partner acquired the existing 205,800-square-foot, five-building campus from BXP. The mixed-phase program includes comprehensive modernization of the existing campus and development of two advanced manufacturing buildings totaling approximately 239,000 square feet. The post CBRE Arranges Debt on Advanced Manufacturing Campus in San Jose’s Golden Triangle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Four Corners Properties acquired 205,800-sq-ft industrial/R&D campus in San Jose Golden Triangle (Jan 2026) from BXP.
CBRE arranged $67.4M five-year bridge loan for mixed-phase development including two new 239,000-sq-ft advanced manufacturing buildings.
CBRE noted 'surging occupier demand and extremely limited supply' positioning Four Corners for value creation.
stories.summary: Four Corners Properties and an institutional investor acquired a 205,800-square-foot industrial/R&D campus in San Jose's Golden Triangle in January 2026 and secured $67.4 million in bridge financing to modernize the existing five buildings and develop two new advanced manufacturing buildings totaling 239,000 square feet. CBRE's debt team highlighted strong occupier demand and constrained supply in the submarket.
stories.impact: Surging occupier demand for advanced manufacturing and R&D space in San Jose Golden Triangle signals sustained job growth in semiconductor, cleantech, and life sciences clusters; this creates upstream demand for workforce housing and long-term rental demand for multifamily in San Jose and nearby submarkets. Tight industrial supply and development activity suggest adjacent residential scarcity, making multifamily development or value-add acquisitions in the metro attractive for 2026–2027.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Closes Sale of Downtown Westfield Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of 251 North Ave. W., a mixed-use property in Westfield, NJ, for $5,260,000. Alan Cafiero, David Cafiero and Damien Rance of Marcus & Millichap exclusively marketed the property on behalf of the seller and procured the private buyer. “Downtown Westfield continues to be one of the most desirable mixed-use investment markets in New Jersey,” said Alan Cafiero, senior managing director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “The combination of a premier downtown location, immediate proximity to the train station and a strong, diverse tenant roster generated significant investor interest in this asset.” The property is a three-story, 17,831-square-foot building on a 0.18-acre lot with direct access to municipal commuter parking. It has nine suites and was renovated in 2014. The rent roll features a diverse mix of service-oriented tenants, including Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, the State of New Jersey, BAYADA Home Health Care and Rooster Spin. The post Marcus & Millichap Closes Sale of Downtown Westfield Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Marcus & Millichap sold 251 North Ave W (Westfield, NJ mixed-use) for $5.26M with diverse service tenants.
17,831-sq-ft, nine-suite property includes Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, State of NJ, BAYADA, Rooster Spin.
Direct access to commuter parking and train station; 2014 renovation; strong investor interest noted.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of a three-story, 17,831-square-foot mixed-use property at 251 North Ave W in Westfield, NJ, for $5.26 million to a private buyer. The property features nine suites with a diverse tenant roster including Columbia Bank, Edward Jones, the State of New Jersey, and BAYADA Home Health Care, plus direct access to municipal parking and the commuter train station.
stories.impact: Westfield's strong downtown mixed-use performance—anchored by commuter rail access and a stable, diversified tenant base—signals durable job and transit-dependent renter demand. The $5.26M sale price reflects investor confidence in suburban mixed-use properties near transit; this validates the value of building multifamily near similar Westfield transit nodes and suggests potential for residential infill near downtown anchors in North Jersey commuter rail markets.

stories.title: Pennrose Cuts Ribbon on Mixed-Income Rentals in Lenox
stories.excerpt: Pennrose held the grand opening of Forge, a new mixed-income rental community for individuals and families in Lenox, MA. The community features 65 apartment units across 13 townhome-style buildings, along with a modern clubhouse and shared amenity spaces. “With few affordable housing options in the area, Forge will provide a high-quality, connected living experience for working individuals and families in Lenox,” said Karmen Cheung, regional VP at Pennrose. “We are proud to partner with the Town to help support its housing production plan and create diverse housing opportunities that will serve as a community asset for many years to come.” In addition to Cheung, speakers at the grand opening ceremony included: Marybeth Mitts, Chair, Lenox Select Board; Don Weber, Chair, Lenox Affordable Housing Trust; State Sen. Paul Mark; State Rep. Leigh Davi; Mark Antonio Wiliams, Regional Director, Office of U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren; Rachel Heller, Executive Director, Massachusetts Housing Partnership; Robert Fraser, President & CEO, MountainOne Bank; Thomas Plihcik, Executive Director, New Lease For Homeless Families; Susan Faas, Forge resident; and Pennrose senior developer Rebecca Schofield. The post Pennrose Cuts Ribbon on Mixed-Income Rentals in Lenox appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Pennrose opened Forge, 65-unit mixed-income community in Lenox, MA (13 townhome-style buildings).
Addresses 'few affordable housing options' in Lenox; partnership with Town to support housing production plan.
Regional leadership and state/federal officials present at grand opening; includes clubhouse and shared amenities.
stories.summary: Pennrose held the grand opening of Forge, a 65-unit mixed-income rental community in Lenox, MA, comprising 13 townhome-style buildings with a clubhouse and shared amenity spaces. The project was developed in partnership with the Town to address a shortage of affordable options and support Lenox's housing production plan.
stories.impact: Lenox's documented shortage of affordable housing and municipal partnership with Pennrose reflects broader Western MA supply constraints and policy support for rental production; this signals receptive local permitting, likely density bonuses or incentives, and strong underlying renter demand. Developers should monitor comparable Berkshires/Western MA markets for similar entitlement-friendly environments and workforce retention opportunities tied to healthcare, tourism, and education anchors.

stories.title: Sack Capital, Align Finance Close Financing for Two Step Up Housing Acquisitions
stories.excerpt: Sack Capital Partners, a San Francisco-based real estate investment and management firm, and Align Finance Partners have closed structured financing for Step Up Housing’s acquisition of two California multifamily communities: Copper Creek, a 268-unit community in Sacramento; and Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit community in Pomona. The combined transactions total 406 units at $91.35 million. Sack will provide asset and property management for both properties. Located at 6430 Verner Ave in Citrus Heights, Copper Creek is a 268-unit garden-style community that traded for $54.65 million. A CBRE team of Marc Ross, Joe McNamara, Claire Holt, Andrew Behrens, and Jesse Weber represented the seller. As previously reported on Connect CRE, Kevin Green, Christopher Zorbas, Joseph Grabiec, Alexander Garcia, Jr., and Gregory Harris of Institutional Property Advisors, a division of Marcus & Millichap, arranged the $36.7-million sale of Terramonte at Foothill. “These two communities give us a foothold in two of California’s most resilient renter markets – greater Sacramento and the Inland Empire gateway of Pomona,” said David Feinberg, Sack Capital Partners managing partner. “Both properties offer the kind of stable in-place cash flow and clear value-add path that we look for, and we’re looking forward to investing in the resident experience at both communities.” The post Sack Capital, Align Finance Close Financing for Two Step Up Housing Acquisitions appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sack Capital and Align Finance closed $91.35M financing for Step Up Housing's 406-unit CA acquisitions.
Copper Creek (268 units, Sacramento, $54.65M); Terramonte at Foothill (138 units, Pomona, $36.7M).
Sack noted acquisitions give 'foothold in two of California's most resilient renter markets' with stable cash flow.
stories.summary: Sack Capital Partners and Align Finance Partners closed structured financing totaling $91.35 million for Step Up Housing's acquisition of two California multifamily communities: Copper Creek, a 268-unit garden-style community in Citrus Heights (Sacramento area) for $54.65 million, and Terramonte at Foothill, a 138-unit community in Pomona, for $36.7 million. Sack will provide asset and property management for both.
stories.impact: Step Up Housing's (a nonprofit acquisition vehicle) strategic focus on Sacramento and Pomona—described as 'resilient renter markets'—with stable in-place cash flow signals institutional confidence in Inland Empire and greater Sacramento as lower-volatility multifamily markets. The $91.35M aggregate deployment suggests ongoing capital availability for value-add/stabilized assets in secondary CA metros despite broader market headwinds; this validates rental demand in these markets and may compress cap rates for similar trophy assets.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $281M C-PACE Loan for Boston Condos
stories.excerpt: The steady climb of commercial property assessed clean energy (C-PACE) financing around the U.S. has made its way to one of Boston’s tallest buildings. Millennium Partners has secured a $281 million C-PACE loan to implement energy efficiency upgrades at the 62-story Winthrop Center in Downtown Boston, the developer announced Friday afternoon. Nuveen Green Capital originated the fixed-rate loan under the Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Massachusetts program which marked the largest C-PACE financing to date in the New England region, according to the lender.,. The condo inventory of the roughly 800,000 square-foot mixed-use building completed in 2023 attracted strong lender competition with many debt funds chasing the loan, according to a source familiar with the transaction. The C-PACE debt closed concurrently with a $575 million commercial mortgage backed securities (CMBS) loan led by Morgan Stanley for the office and retail portion of the tower according to a presale report from Moody’s. CoStar first reported the MP Trust 2026-WTRP single-asset-single-borrower deal for Boston’s largest building in the city’s financial district. The combined $856 million debt package takes out a prior construction loan from Cale Street in October 2020 after the London firm stepped in following another bank who backed out during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, according to sources. “We were honored to partner with MassDevelopment to recapitalize the largest C-PACE-financed project in New England, one that has helped reshape downtown Boston with state-of-the-art, energy-efficient residences,” Mike Doty, senior director of originations for NGC, said in a statement. Christopher M. Jeffries, founder of Millennium Partners, said in a statement that the C-PACE loan “recognizes the investments we have made in energy efficiency while providing long-term capital that supports the building’s enduring performance.” The PACE Massachusetts program was updated in June
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closed $281M C-PACE loan (fixed-rate) for Millennium Partners' Winthrop Center, Boston.
62-story, 800,000-sq-ft mixed-use (condo/office) completed 2023; largest C-PACE financing in New England to date.
Concurrent $575M CMBS loan from Morgan Stanley; strong lender competition noted for condo-heavy asset.
stories.summary: Millennium Partners secured a $281 million fixed-rate C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital to fund energy efficiency upgrades at Boston's 62-story Winthrop Center, a completed 800,000-square-foot mixed-use building. The financing is the largest C-PACE in New England and closed alongside a $575 million CMBS loan led by Morgan Stanley, with strong lender competition for the condo-heavy asset.
stories.impact: The record C-PACE financing size and concurrent CMBS deployment for Winthrop Center signals that Boston's completed mixed-use condo/office assets are re-attracting capital; however, the reliance on two financing tranches (PACE + CMBS) and mention of 'many debt funds chasing the loan' suggests competition for trophy assets may be masking tighter conditions for secondary or multifamily-only projects. Multifamily developers should note that mixed-use/condo buildings are capturing outsized capital allocation in Boston; pure residential may face relative disadvantage.

stories.title: Nalcorp, Clipper Equity Buy Coney Island Oceanfront Development Site for $20M
stories.excerpt: Fancy a trip to the Boardwalk? A pair of New York-based real estate development and investment firms — Nalcorp and Clipper Equity — have acquired a land parcel at 2015 Boardwalk West, an oceanfront development in Coney Island, Brooklyn, from seller Bath Site LLC for $20 million, broker TerraCRG announced Friday. The parking lot property, which spans 69,530 square feet and has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage, seems to be part of a larger ongoing development on the site. Permits were filed in 2024 to build a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at 2015 Boardwalk West. The larger parcel of land home to the development was purchased in 2006 by the City Investment Fund — a real estate private equity vehicle launched by the Fisher Brothers and Morgan Stanley — from Thor Equities for $90 million. Following the 2006 sale, the larger parcel was subdivided into six separate tax lots, including the one part of this most recent transaction, which is called Block 7072, Lot 6. Bath Site LLC — an entity comprising Georgica Green Ventures and its nonprofit partner RiseBoro Community Partnership — acquired this property in July 2024 for $10.4 million. Dan Marks and Daniel Lebor from TerraCRG represented Bath Site LLC in this transaction. The firm did not disclose the names of the brokers who represented the buyers. The buyers did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while the seller could not be reached for comment. “Coney Island has become one of New York City’s most exciting waterfront growth stories,” Marks said in a statement. “Ongoing public and private investment has transformed the area into one of the city’s most compelling waterfront markets. bullets: Nalcorp and Clipper Equity acquired 69,530-sq-ft oceanfront parking lot (Coney Island) for $20M from Bath Site LLC.
247 feet of Boardwalk frontage; permits filed in 2024 for 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building at site.
Larger parcel subdivided into six tax lots by City Investment Fund (Fisher Brothers/Morgan Stanley partnership, 2006).
stories.summary: Nalcorp and Clipper Equity purchased a 69,530-square-foot oceanfront parking lot at 2015 Boardwalk West in Coney Island, Brooklyn, for $20 million. The property has 247 feet of Boardwalk frontage and is part of a larger development where permits were filed in 2024 for a 23-story, 202-unit mixed-use building.
stories.impact: Oceanfront Coney Island land trading hands at $20M for a 202-unit mixed-use development signals sustained investor interest in Brooklyn waterfront development and confidence in Coney Island rental demand recovery. The presence of institutional sponsors (Fisher Brothers' City Investment Fund held the larger parcel since 2006) and current developer enthusiasm suggests multi-year lease-up strength and reduced downside risk; multifamily developers should monitor Coney Island pipeline for absorption and pricing trends as a bellwether for Brooklyn waterfront competitiveness.

stories.title: Survey: 61% of Investors Hold Negative Multifamily Outlook in 2026, Per Berkadia
stories.excerpt: Housing isn’t making anyone happy these days. In a survey of more than 100 principals and executives across private real estate investment firms, Berkadia found that 61 percent of respondents characterized their outlook for the multifamily market in the second half of 2026 as negative due to capital markets volatility, Commercial Observer can first report. Meanwhile, 52 percent said that the asset class performed worse in the first half of the year than they had anticipated. “Six months ago, investors were very optimistic that [volatility] was going to fade and transaction activity was going to accelerate,” said Josh Bodin, senior vice president of capital markets strategy and trading at Berkadia, in a conversation with CO. “Instead, the operating environment has remained a lot more uncertain, interest rate volatility has persisted and property performance has stayed softer than expected,” he added. Bond yields have been high for most of 2026. The 10-Year Treasury currently sits at 4.7 percent, its highest levels since 2023, while the 30-Year Treasury sits at 5.2 percent, a 20-year high. In a separate report, CBRE found that first-quarter investment sales in multifamily hit $29.5 billion, a 6 percent decline year-over-year, while the second quarter saw a rebound of investment sales activity to $34.9 billion (that total was still down by 2.7 percent year-over-year). However, Bodin emphasized these metrics and investors’ sentiments haven’t translated into a loss of confidence in multifamily as an asset class, but has instead changed how investors view execution risk. To this end, Berkadia’s survey found that 82 percent of investors plan to expand their portfolios in the coming months and that 83 percent expect market conditions to improve by late 2027. “On the tailwinds side, near-term, supply deliveries are beginning to moderate in many markets, capital remains really available for well-positioned assets and investors increasingly expect conditions to improve,” said
bullets: Berkadia survey: 61% of multifamily investors hold negative outlook for H2 2026 due to market volatility.
52% say asset performance in H1 2026 was worse than expected; uncertainty persists on rates and operations.
10-Year Treasury at 4.7% (highest since 2023); 30-Year at 5.2% (20-year high); bond yields elevated.
stories.summary: In a Berkadia survey of over 100 real estate investment principals, 61 percent reported a negative outlook for multifamily in the second half of 2026, citing capital markets volatility and persistent uncertainty. Fifty-two percent said first-half performance was worse than anticipated, with interest rate volatility and softer property operating performance dragging sentiment. Treasury yields remain elevated at 4.7% (10-year) and 5.2% (30-year), the highest in recent years.
stories.impact: A 61% negative sentiment and elevated Treasury yields (4.7–5.2%) directly suppress cap rates, increase underwriting hurdle rates, and freeze transaction activity; this tightens acquisition windows and forces developers to prioritize high-growth markets and strong sponsors with lower cost of capital. The gap between H1 expectations and H1 reality signals that rent growth is lagging forecasts—a red flag for speculative development. Conservative underwriting with lower pro-forma rent growth is now essential; repricing and slower deployments will likely persist through H2 2026.

stories.title: St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort Secures $263M Refi After Special Servicing
stories.excerpt: Fortress Investment Group has rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company (ARTIC)’s St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing, supplying a $263 million loan to refinance the oceanfront property. The New York-based lender assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new debt backing the 213-room property in Bal Harbour, Fla., north of Miami Beach, according to public mortgage documents, which valued the asset at $311 million. The new financing comes nearly a year after a $188 million commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) loan tied to the resort headed to special servicing as the financing was set to mature. Although the loan remained current and the resort maintained a debt service coverage ratio above break-even, its cash flow in 2024 was about half of 2021 levels, the year it had secured the debt. The lender, Column Financial, wanted ARTIC to buy a replacement interest rate cap, which it had yet to secure, Morningstar reported. ARTIC, which is run by a member of the Qatari ruling family, had purchased the resort for $213 million in 2014, three years after it was completed. The complex, which features three 27-story towers at 9703 Collins Avenue, houses two pools, a 14,000-square-foot spa, five dining outposts, 13,000 square feet of event space as well as a condo component. The hotel owner and condo owners have sparred. In 2024, the condo association sued ARTIC over alleged building defects, safety hazards, and financial mismanagement. The parties settled the suit a year later. Fortress Investment Group and ARTIC did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Fortress Investment Group refinanced St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort (213 rooms, Bal Harbour, FL) with $263M loan.
Resort exited special servicing; Fortress assumed $188M existing debt and added $70M new debt; asset valued at $311M.
Cash flow in 2024 was ~50% of 2021 levels; prior CMBS loan matured; rate cap procurement issue noted.
stories.summary: Fortress Investment Group rescued Al Rayyan Tourism Investment Company's St. Regis Bal Harbour Resort out of special servicing with a $263 million refinance. The oceanfront property in Bal Harbour was valued at $311 million; Fortress assumed $188 million in existing debt and added $70 million in new capital. The resort's 2024 cash flow declined to roughly half of 2021 levels, prompting the special servicing when the prior CMBS loan matured.
stories.impact: The St. Regis Bal Harbour distress and rescue signals hospitality asset stress in South Florida resort markets despite strong real estate fundamentals; the 50% cash-flow decline since 2021 suggests yield compression from elevated financing costs and softer post-pandemic occupancy. While hospitality is outside multifamily core, the tight financing conditions and lender distress in South Florida—even for trophy trophy assets—presage capital tightness affecting all real estate classes; multifamily developers in Miami/Bal Harbour should expect higher debt costs and greater equity requirements for new development.

stories.title: First Pioneer Properties Buys Queens Retail Center for $24M
stories.excerpt: New York-based real estate management and development firm First Pioneer Properties, along with ABS Partners Real Estate, has acquired a Queens retail center from Levy Properties for $23.5 million, property records made public Thursday show. The one-story property at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside is currently home to an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store. Jennifer Markowitz of Levy Properties signed the deal for the seller, while Suresh Sani, owner of First Pioneer Properties, signed for the buyers. ABS seems to act as a frequent co-investor and partner of First Pioneer Properties. It’s unclear who brokered the deal. The buyers and seller did not immediately respond to Commercial Observer’s requests for comment. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet, according to data from PincusCo. The buyers’ intentions for the property are unclear, but Queens has been awash with multifamily developments lately. This month, Wells Fargo provided a $175 million construction loan to the Domain Companies for a 429-unit mixed-income housing development at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in Astoria. Also this month, LMXD and BedRock Real Estate Partners closed on a $250 million loan to build a housing development at 35-10 Steinway Street in Astoria. Earlier this summer, another Queens retail property changed hands when Punia & Marx Real Estate sold the Whitestone Shopping Center at 153-15 Cross Island Parkway for $56 million. Meanwhile, a historic Queens bowling alley — Whitestone Lanes — at 30-05 Whitestone Expressway in Flushing — sold for $45 million in June as part of a major multifamily development project coming to the area. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners acquired retail center (Bayside, Queens) from Levy Properties for $23.5M.
213-04 Northern Boulevard: 24,000 sq ft built + 74,350 sq ft air rights (98,478 sq ft total buildable).
Current tenants: urgent care medical office and baby store; Queens has 'been awash with multifamily developments lately.'
stories.summary: First Pioneer Properties and ABS Partners Real Estate acquired a one-story retail center at 213-04 Northern Boulevard in Bayside, Queens, from Levy Properties for $23.5 million. The property has 24,000 square feet of built space and 74,350 square feet of additional air rights for a total of 98,478 buildable square feet. Current tenants include an urgent care medical office and Bebeang Baby Store.
stories.impact: The substantial air rights (74,350 sq ft) at this Bayside retail center signal zoning for vertical development; combined with the article's observation that 'Queens has been awash with multifamily developments,' this suggests First Pioneer may be repositioning the site for residential conversion or mixed-use development. The purchase price ($23.5M) for buildable entitlements on 98,478 sq ft implies ~$238/buildable sq ft—a value-add signal. Developers should monitor Bayside/Flushing for upzoning activity and pipeline conversions; retail-to-residential transitions in Queens may indicate softer retail fundamentals but robust rental demand and zoning willingness to support residential supply.
